articles.title: IBM quantum computer solves classically intractable problem in 15 minutes
articles.summary: IBM and University of Chicago researchers have completed a quantum computation that leading classical methods could not practically reproduce. The system used 70 error-corrected logical qubits and finished the task in roughly 15 minutes while also providing statistical evidence that the result was reliable.

articles.title: OpenAI keeps bulldozing mathematicians
articles.summary: In a chaotic few months, OpenAI has demonstrated it can do two things with remarkable consistency: make impressive breakthroughs in mathematics, then colossally screw up announcing them. OpenAI is now trying to do better. Somehow, it has botched that too. OpenAI's latest attempt to repair fractured relations with a mathematical community it has repeatedly alienated […]

articles.title: Quantum computing’s “dark horse” just proved it can go universal
articles.summary: Researchers have shown that exotic quantum particles called non-Abelian anyons can perform the full range of operations needed for universal quantum computing. Using 54 qubits on Quantinuum’s H2 processor, they combined braiding and fusion to unlock capabilities that braiding alone could not provide.

articles.title: Scientists just made quantum computer operations 1,000 times faster
articles.summary: Researchers have found a way to perform certain quantum operations more than 1,000 times faster, cutting thousands of repeated control cycles down to just one. The advance could reduce errors and bring reliable, fault-tolerant quantum computers closer to reality.

articles.title: A “quantum bath” puts quantum entanglement on autopilot
articles.summary: Physicists have demonstrated a new way to entangle distant quantum bits without the constant measurements and active control normally required. The team created a “quantum bath,” a shared environment filled with correlated microwave photons that automatically pushes separated qubits into an entangled state and helps keep them there. The experiment confirms a theoretical prediction made more than 20 years ago and could offer a simpler way to connect modules in future quantum computers.

articles.title: Peak XV ups Surge seed investment ceiling to $5M, unveils 18-startup cohort
articles.summary: Thirteen of the 18 startups in Peak XV’s latest Surge cohort are targeting global markets, while more than half are based in India.

articles.title: Source: Inference provider Modal Labs closing in on $750M round at $15.75B valuation
articles.summary: The new financing is expected to more than triples the AI infrastructure startup's valuation from just four months ago.

articles.title: AMD will acquire Fei-Fei Li’s World Labs for $8.2 billion
articles.summary: The acquisition will see World Labs founder Fei-Fei Li join AMD as executive vice president and chief scientist.

articles.title: The AI boom took over Climate Week and not everyone is happy about it
articles.summary: Just like the rest of the U.S., data centers and AI are dividing climate tech founders and investors.

articles.title: Seeing the unseen, coloring anime: How AI and physics are shaping the future of imaging, Q&A
articles.summary: Cameras have long been regarded as tools for capturing what the human eye can see. But that assumption may soon be challenged.

articles.title: Diamond quantum sensor enables AC and DC current ratio checks in one setup
articles.summary: Researchers at AIST, in collaboration with the Institute of Science Tokyo and the National Institutes for Quantum Science and Technology, have developed a "current comparator" that uses diamond quantum sensors to accurately evaluate both AC and DC current ratios with the same device setup. Their work is published in the journal Scientific Reports.

articles.title: AMD is acquiring AI company World Labs in a deal worth more than $8 billion
articles.summary: AMD announced today that it's acquiring World Labs, an AI research lab co-founded by the prominent researcher Dr. Fei-Fei Li, in an all-stock deal worth approximately $8.2 billion. World Labs launched in 2024 and was valued at $1 billion in a matter of months. The startup launched its first commercial product, a world generation model […]

articles.title: AI is supercharging hacking, and your local hospitals and banks aren’t ready
articles.summary: In March, Janice Malone began getting calls about suspicious activity from her nonprofit organization, Vivian's Door. Vivian's Door, headquartered in Alabama, typically provided training, resources, and community to underserved and minority-owned businesses. The work sometimes put it in close contact with these companies' financial data, which was stored on its systems. But suddenly, concerned callers […]

articles.title: Walmart won’t hike prices based on your shopping history, CEO says
articles.summary: Walmart says it won't change product prices based on your personal information or the time of day, as reported earlier by The Wall Street Journal. In a letter to customers, Walmart CEO John Furner writes that the company's switch to digital shelf labels is meant to save store associates time, rather than dynamically change prices. […]

articles.title: The SaaSpocalypse that wasn’t, with Atlassian CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes
articles.summary: Today, I’m talking with Mike Cannon-Brookes, who is cofounder and CEO of Atlassian.  Atlassian is one of those companies that every other company runs on — it makes important platform tools like Jira and Trello that allow people to organize and manage big teams, create shared databases of company information, and generally allow work to […]

articles.title: Engram is a sampler that turns broken AI hallucinations into music
articles.summary: Music startup Thoughtful Things has just launched the Kickstarter campaign for its first instrument, Engram. It's a sampler and groovebox that uses AI to mangle incoming audio and even hallucinate completely new sounds. This isn't Suno in a box, though. This isn't a "push-button, get-song" device, aimed at creating something that sounds ready for top-40 […]

articles.title: MIT’s tiny flying robot gets 450% faster with AI
articles.summary: A new AI control system lets MIT’s tiny flying robot move with insect-like agility, boosting its speed by about 450 percent and allowing it to pull off 10 somersaults in 11 seconds. The technology could eventually enable miniature robots to search earthquake rubble and navigate dangerous spaces that conventional drones cannot reach.

articles.title: The shape behind the Einstein problem just revealed strange new physics
articles.summary: A mathematical shape famous for covering a surface without ever repeating has revealed an unexpected ability to twist light into unusual chiral patterns. The discovery could lead to new ways of controlling light, polarization, and advanced optical devices.

articles.title: AI uncovers hidden Ozempic side effects across 400,000 Reddit posts
articles.summary: AI analysis of 400,000 Reddit posts found that users of drugs such as Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound reported unexpected symptoms including menstrual changes, chills, hot flashes, and fatigue. Researchers cannot say the medications caused these problems, but the patterns may reveal overlooked signals worth studying.

articles.title: Tiny nanolaser could cut computer energy use in half
articles.summary: Scientists have created an ultra-small nanolaser that could eventually allow microchips to transmit information with light instead of electricity, potentially making computers faster while cutting energy use roughly in half. Thousands of the lasers could fit on a single chip, opening possibilities for more efficient data centers, smartphones, and advanced medical sensors.

articles.title: NASA just used satellites and debris to navigate without GPS
articles.summary: NASA has successfully tested a system that allows satellites to navigate without GPS by using other spacecraft and debris as landmarks in orbit. In just three days, FALCON also improved the known orbits of more than 200 space objects completely autonomously.

articles.title: Scientists turn DNA into a memory device that uses 100x less power
articles.summary: Researchers combined synthetic DNA with a semiconductor to create an ultra-low-power memory device capable of storing and processing information in the same place. The bio-hybrid technology could eventually help make AI systems and next-generation computers far more energy efficient.

articles.title: Research provides evidence-based practical tools to reduce ultra-low temperature freezer energy costs
articles.summary: A cross-functional team comprised of researchers, supply chain management, and facilities leadership, at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF), has developed and tested a practical approach to help research institutions identify energy-intensive ultra-low temperature (ULT) freezers, prioritize replacements, and forecast potential energy and cost savings.

articles.title: Saltwater sensor turns touch into electrical signals like skin, with prosthetic potential
articles.summary: You pick up a fragile glass from the table. Without thinking about it, you feel its surface against your fingertips and continuously adjust your grip. You hold it firmly enough to keep it from slipping out of your hand, but not so tightly that it breaks.

articles.title: Self-powered artificial synapse combines sensing and memory in flexible electronics
articles.summary: Neuromorphic devices, which are designed to emulate aspects of biological neural networks, are promising candidates for low-power, intelligent sensing technologies, including wearable applications.

articles.title: Pressurized wind tunnel experiments could help wind farms generate more power
articles.summary: The world needs more wind energy. But anyone designing new wind turbines or trying to squeeze more power out of existing ones faces a stiff challenge when testing new approaches. That's because the atmosphere is a tough place for a controlled experiment.

articles.title: Glowing paint that maps air pressure could improve the design of future aircraft
articles.summary: When engineers design a new aircraft, they need to know exactly how air flows over every surface. The pressure distribution must be controlled, or fuel efficiency, handling and even structural safety can be affected.

articles.title: Misleading AI-generated summaries can distort human memory
articles.summary: AI-generated summaries are becoming increasingly prevalent—from news article previews to workplace meeting transcriptions to high-stakes settings like police body camera footage—despite studies showing that AI can generate misleading or inaccurate information.

articles.title: AI chatbots give us a narrow slice of knowledge: Researchers warn of 'knowledge collapse'
articles.summary: For many of us, "Let me just ask the chatbot" has become an everyday phrase. Where we used to turn to Google to find information, AI chatbots have become a common way to get answers to everything from what to make for dinner and how to word a difficult email to the boss to what it means when interest rates rise.

articles.title: Greater job security can make inventors less creative
articles.summary: When Apple recently presented its (rather pricey) new folding phone, one of the questions hovering over the launch—and in particular its new CEO, John Ternus—was whether the technology giant can recover its famously innovative magic touch.
